programmes.title: AI Literacy & Prompt Engineering
programmes.skills: Prompt design, fact-checking, privacy, responsible AI
programmes.goal: Use generative AI effectively and verify its output.
programmes.audience: Students, professionals and educators. No coding required.
programmes.cap: Produce a verified AI-assisted research portfolio with a prompt log, evidence matrix and risk register.
modules: AI fundamentals
Distinguish generative AI, search and conventional software.
Compare a search result and AI answer; explain limitations.
Prompt design
Construct clear instructions and evaluate improvements.
Create three progressively improved prompts and compare results.
Research and verification
Verify factual claims against primary sources.
Check five AI-generated claims using a source matrix.
Privacy and responsible use
Identify unsafe disclosure, bias and misuse.
Review a fictional workplace AI policy and recommend safeguards.
Practical AI workflows
Design a repeatable human-reviewed workflow.
Submit a workflow, before/after outputs and independent quality check.
sample: An AI assistant gives you a convincing statistic but no source.
What should you do?
Publish it immediately
Verify it against a reliable primary source
Ask it to sound more confident
Verify original evidence before publishing. If you cannot confirm the claim, remove it or disclose uncertainty.

sample: A service sells for R500, variable cost is R200 and monthly fixed costs are R3,000.
How many sales cover fixed costs?
6 sales
10 sales
15 sales
Contribution is R300 per sale. R3,000 ÷ R300 = 10 sales, assuming costs remain constant.

Send your banking password

sample: Daily sales are R100, R120, R130, R150 and R1,000. The mean is R300 and the median is R130.
Which measure best represents a typical day in this skewed dataset?
Median, R130
Maximum, R1,000
Mean, R300 without explanation
The median is less influenced by an extreme value. Report both when useful and explain the outlier.
